Key Characteristics & Etiology: Placental shallow trophoblastic invasion & endothelial dysfunction
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Systemic vasospasm and endothelial leak leading to multi-organ impairment
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: BP >=140/90 after 20wks + proteinuria; Red Flags: severe headache, epigastric pain, hyperreflexia, clonus, seizures
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Urine PCR >=30 mg/mmol; Aspirin 75-150mg prophylaxis; Oral/IV Labetalol; IV MgSO4 (4g load then 1g/h); Delivery

Key Characteristics & Etiology: High hCG cross-stimulating thyroid TSH receptors in early pregnancy / hyperemesis
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Elevated free T4 with suppressed TSH without autoantibodies or goitre
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe nausea, vomiting, mild palpitations, no ophthalmopathy or goitre
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Suppressed TSH with mildly elevated FT4; TPO negative; Self-limiting (resolves by 14-18wks); Reassurance (no antithyroid drugs)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Autoimmune stimulation of TSH receptor by TSH-receptor antibodies (TRAb)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Excess thyroid hormone production leading to maternal hypermetabolism and fetal thyrotoxicosis risk
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Goitre, ophthalmopathy (exophthalmos), tachycardia, tremor, heat intolerance
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Suppressed TSH, elevated FT4/FT3, positive TRAb; Propylthiouracil (PTU) in 1st trimester (switch to Carbimazole in 2nd/3rd)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Primary adrenal insufficiency decompensation under stress
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Inadequate cortisol/aldosterone production leading to severe hypovolemia and vascular collapse
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe vomiting, dehydration, hypotension, abdominal pain, fever
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia; Immediate IV Hydrocortisone 100mg stat + aggressive IV normal saline resuscitation

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Catecholamine-secreting chromaffin cell tumor of adrenal medulla
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Paroxysmal release of epinephrine/norepinephrine causing severe vasoconstriction and hypertensive crisis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Classic triad: episodic headache, diaphoresis (sweating), and severe hypertension
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Elevated plasma/urinary free metanephrines; MRI abdomen; Preoperative Alpha-blockade (Phenoxybenzamine/Doxazosin) for 10-14 days before surgery

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Primary hyperaldosteronism (aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Excess aldosterone causes renal sodium/water retention and urinary potassium wasting
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: New-onset hypertension, muscular weakness, fatigue, hypokalemia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Suppressed plasma renin activity with elevated serum aldosterone; Potassium replacement + Spironolactone (or surgical excision)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Increased maternal thyroxine demand & TBG elevation in early pregnancy
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Inadequate maternal thyroid hormone production to meet increased gestational demand
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Fatigue, weight gain, constipation, cold intolerance (often subtle)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Elevated TSH (>2.5 mU/L 1st trim / >3.0 2nd-3rd) with normal FT4; Increase Levothyroxine dose by 25-50% upon pregnancy confirmation

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Virchow's triad in pregnancy (hypercoagulability, venous stasis, pelvic vein compression)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Thrombus formation in deep limb or pelvic veins risk of detachment to PE
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Unilateral leg swelling (>2cm differential), calf tenderness, erythema, lower abdominal pain
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Compression duplex ultrasound (1st line); MRI pelvis if iliac thrombosis suspected; Therapeutic LMWH (Enoxaparin 1mg/kg BD)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Detached venous thromboembolus occluding pulmonary arterial circulation
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Sudden increase in right ventricular afterload and severe ventilation-perfusion mismatch
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, hypoxia, tachycardia, collapse (massive PE - Red Flag)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: CXR followed by V/Q scan or CTPA (D-dimer NOT used); Therapeutic LMWH; Thrombolysis (IV Alteplase) for massive PE with collapse

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Airway hyperresponsiveness triggered by viral infection or non-compliance
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Bronchospasm, mucosal edema, and mucus plugging impairing maternal/fetal gas exchange
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Dyspnea, wheezing, tachypnoea; Red Flags: PEFR <50% predicted, inability to complete sentences, silent chest
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: PEFR measurement; ABG (PaCO2 >=4.0 kPa indicates fatigue); High-flow O2 (target 94-98%); Nebulized Salbutamol/Ipratropium; IV Hydrocortisone

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Seizure disorder in pregnancy; increased drug clearance and volume of distribution
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Breakthrough seizure activity risking maternal aspiration, hypoxia, and fetal distress
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Generalised tonic-clonic seizures, post-ictal confusion; Red Flags: status epilepticus, SUDEP risk
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Therapeutic drug monitoring; High-dose Folic acid (5mg daily); Lamotrigine / Levetiracetam preferred; Valproate strictly avoided

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Thrombosis of dural venous sinuses in puerperium (hypercoagulable state)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Impaired cerebral venous drainage leading to venous infarction and intracranial hypertension
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe persistent progressive headache, vomiting, seizures, focal neurological signs, papilloedema
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: CT brain with venography / MRI brain with MRV (1st line); Full therapeutic dose LMWH anticoagulation

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Transient neuroendocrine fluctuations following rapid post-delivery hormone withdrawal
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Rapid drop in circulating estrogen and progesterone triggering transient emotional lability
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Tearfulness, emotional lability, mild anxiety, irritability developing days 3-5 postpartum
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Clinical diagnosis; Reassurance and supportive care; Self-limiting (resolves within 10-14 days without medication)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Perinatal mood disorder; 50% recurrence rate in women with previous history
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Persistent deficits in central monoaminergic neurotransmission post-delivery
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Low mood, anhedonia, early morning awakening, guilt, inability to cope, feeling hopeless
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS); Sertraline (safest in breastfeeding) + CBT; Specialist perinatal mental health referral

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Severe psychiatric illness; high association with personal/family history of bipolar disorder
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Acute neurochemical dysregulation in immediate postpartum period (1 in 1000 incidence)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Delusions (e.g. baby possessed), hallucinations, severe agitation, mania, thoughts of harm
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Emergency Psychiatric Evaluation; Mandatory immediate admission to Mother and Baby Unit (MBU); Antipsychotics + Mood stabilizers

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Autoimmune disease characterized by polyclonal B-cell activation & complement deficiency
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Immune complex deposition in renal glomeruli causing inflammation and proteinuria
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Malar rash, joint pain (90%), proteinuria, hypertension, renal flare
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: ANA & Anti-dsDNA positive, low C3/C4; Delay pregnancy until 6 months of stable remission; Aspirin + Hydroxychloroquine

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Urethral hypermobility or intrinsic sphincter deficiency under increased intra-abdominal pressure
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Involuntary urine leakage on coughing, sneezing, laughing, or physical exertion
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Involuntary urine loss during physical stress without prior urge
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Clinical diagnosis; Cough stress test; Urodynamic studies; Pelvic Floor Muscle Training (PFMT) >=3 months 1st line; Surgical Colposuspension

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Involuntary detrusor muscle contractions during bladder filling
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Urgency-predominant incontinence accompanied by frequency and nocturia
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Sudden imperative desire to void, involuntary leakage preceded by urgency
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Urodynamic cystometry (detrusor overactivity); Bladder Training >=6 weeks 1st line; Anticholinergics (Solifenacin) or Mirabegron

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Levator ani muscle & uterosacral ligament weakness (cystocele, rectocele, enterocele, procidentia)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Herniation of pelvic organs past vaginal introitus; Procidentia = complete uterine/vaginal descent
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Pelvic fullness, draggy backache, vaginal bulge, decubitus ulcer on exposed cervix
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Clinical POP-Q exam; Ring Pessary + Topical Oestrogen 1st line (especially in frail elderly); Surgery: Colporrhaphy / Colpoclesis

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Chronic autoimmune inflammatory dermatosis of vulva and perineum
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Epidermal hyperkeratosis, dermal hyalinization/fibrosis, loss of rete ridges without atypia
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Intense chronic vulval pruritus, dyspareunia, figure-of-eight porcelain-white plaques
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Vulval punch biopsy; Ultra-potent topical corticosteroid (Clobetasol propionate 0.05%) for 3 months

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Extramammary intraepidermal adenocarcinoma of vulva
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Intraepidermal proliferation of large pale atypical Paget cells
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Chronic eczematous vulval lesion, burning, severe itching, erythematous plaque with white scales
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Vulval biopsy: CK7 positive, HER2 positive, CEA positive; Wide local excision / Vulvectomy + screen for underlying malignancy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Persistently elevated/rising hCG following molar evacuation or non-molar pregnancy (choriocarcinoma)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Malignant proliferation of trophoblastic tissue with vascular invasion and distant metastases (lung)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Persistent vaginal bleeding, high hCG, pulmonary lesions on imaging
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Serum hCG monitoring; FIGO risk scoring: Low-risk (score 0-6) -> Single-agent Methotrexate; High-risk (score >=7) -> Multi-agent EMA/CO chemotherapy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Invasive cervical carcinoma linked to high-risk hrHPV 16 & 18 (71% of cases)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: High-risk HPV E6/E7 oncogenes inhibit p53 and Rb tumor suppressors leading to invasive growth
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Postcoital bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, purulent discharge, pelvic pain
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Cervical biopsy; MRI pelvis + PET-CT (most accurate for nodal metastasis); Stage IB3 (bulky >=4cm) -> Primary Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma (High-grade serous/clear cell linked to Lynch syndrome)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Pelvic extension of ovarian tumor implanting on uterus and/or fallopian tubes (Stage IIA)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Abdominal bloating, early satiety, pelvic mass, positive peritoneal washings
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: CA-125; Pelvic TVUS; CT Abdomen/Pelvis; Staging laparotomy + Cytoreductive debulking surgery + Carboplatin/Paclitaxel
